name: loaded_language
definition: Using specific words and phrases with strong emotional implications (either positive or negative) to influence an audience.

name: name_calling
definition: Labeling the object of the propaganda campaign as either something the target audience fears, hates, finds undesirable or loves, praises.

name: repetition
definition: Repeating the same message over and over again so that the audience will eventually accept it.
example: I still have a dream. It is a dream deeply rooted in the American dream.

name: exaggeration
definition: Either representing something in an excessive manner: making things larger, better, worse, or making something seem less important or smaller than it actually is.
example: We're going to have unbelievable intelligence

name: doubt
definition: Questioning the credibility of someone or something.
example: Can the same be said for the Obama Administration?

name: appeal_to_fear
definition: Seeking to build support for an idea by instilling anxiety and/or panic in the population towards an alternative, possibly based on preconceived judgments.
example: either we go to war or we will perish

name: flag_waving
definition: Playing on strong national feeling (or with respect to any group, e.g., race, gender, political preference) to justify or promote an action or idea.
example: Mueller attempts to stop the will of We the People!!!

name: causal_oversimplification
definition: Assuming a single cause or reason when there are multiple causes behind an issue. Includes scapegoating: transfer of blame to one person or group without investigating the complexities.
example: If France had not declared war on Germany then World War II would have never happened.

name: slogans
definition: A brief and striking phrase that may include labeling and stereotyping. Slogans tend to act as emotional appeals.

name: appeal_to_authority
definition: Stating that a claim is true simply because a valid authority or expert on the issue said it was true, without any other supporting evidence. Includes testimonials from non-experts.
example: Monsignor Lantheaume confirmed that Vigano said the truth. That's all.

name: black_and_white
definition: Presenting two alternative options as the only possibilities when in fact more possibilities exist. Extreme case: telling the audience exactly what actions to take, eliminating any other choice.
example: There is no alternative to war

name: thought_terminating
definition: Words or phrases that discourage critical thought and meaningful discussion on a topic. Typically short, generic sentences that offer seemingly simple answers to complex questions.
example: I do not really see any problems there. It is what it is.

name: whataboutism
definition: Whataboutism: discrediting an opponent by charging hypocrisy without disproving their argument. Straw man: substituting an opponent's proposition with a similar weaker one. Red herring: introducing irrelevant material to divert attention.
example: President Trump — who himself avoided military service — keeps beating the war drums over North Korea.

name: bandwagon
definition: Bandwagon: persuading the audience to take action because everyone else is doing it. Reductio ad Hitlerum: persuading an audience to disapprove an idea by suggesting it is popular with groups held in contempt.
example: Do you know who else was doing that? Hitler!
